speaker: narrator
text: You own nearly every onion in the city, and they're rotting.

speaker: narrator
text: Eight pounds of onion for every person in Chicago.

speaker: narrator
text: Dump them, and the price collapses.

speaker: narrator
text: So farmers buy some, if you lock up the rest.

speaker: narrator
text: You've sold onions by promising not to sell onions.

speaker: narrator
text: You sell futures: promises to deliver onions later, at today's price.

speaker: narrator
text: If onions get cheaper, you keep the difference.

speaker: narrator
text: The story goes the empty bag cost twenty.

speaker: narrator
text: Tip the onions out, and you've doubled your money.

speaker: narrator
text: The men behind it: Vincent Kosuga and Sam Siegel.

speaker: narrator
text: The government ruled they'd manipulated the price.
